steps: Agree with your planning leads which of your Planning record types, such as campaigns, link to the GenStudio workspace's record types, in a mapping sheet.
Connect your Planning record types to the GenStudio workspace's record types, so each plan points to the products and personas its content is generated from.
Connect the agreed Planning record types to GenStudio Brands, in whichever workspace they sit, so each plan also points to its brand.
Test the links on sample plans with your planning leads, check that a change made in one app shows in the other, and record their sign-off.
deliverables: Planning record types linked to the GenStudio workspace
Planning record types connected to GenStudio Brands
Record type mapping sheet
Sample plan test results
asks: A planning lead who owns your record types and approves each link
Administrator access to Workfront Planning and GenStudio for Performance Marketing
risk: Plans linked to the wrong brand or persona: we agree each link in a mapping sheet and test it on sample plans before your teams rely on it.
outcome: Each of your plans in Workfront Planning points to the brand, products and personas its content is generated from in GenStudio for Performance Marketing.

steps: Agree with your planning and project leads which Planning record types connect to Workfront projects, portfolios, programs, companies or groups, and the one-to-many rule for each.
Connect each record type to its agreed Workfront object type first, since individual records and objects can be connected only after that.
Bring in the lookup fields your leaders need on each record type, such as the dates and status of the connected work.
Link a sample of existing records to their work, check it with each lead, then link the rest and record their sign-off.
deliverables: Record types connected to Workfront object types
Lookup fields for your leaders
Existing records linked to their work
Connection map with one-to-many rules
asks: Planning and project leads who can agree which records connect to which work
A list of the lookup fields your leaders want to see on each plan
Access to Workfront Planning and to the Workfront projects, programs and portfolios involved
risk: Records linked to the wrong work: we agree each rule with your leads and check a sample of links with them before we link the rest.
outcome: Each of your plans in Workfront Planning is linked to the Workfront work that delivers it, with the dates and status your leaders need.

steps: Agree with your project leads which record types, such as campaigns, should create a Workfront project, program or portfolio, and which template each one uses.
Review the project templates that capture your repeatable processes with your project leads, so each new project follows the agreed process.
Configure the automations on the agreed record types to create the Workfront work from a record and connect the new object back to that record.
Test each automation on sample records, check the new work and its link back, and record the results for your sign-off.
deliverables: Automations on the agreed record types
Record of the template each automation uses
Test results and sign-off record
asks: Project leads who decide which records create work and which template applies
The project templates your teams use today, or the processes to capture
risk: Projects created from the wrong template or left unlinked: we test each automation on sample records and check the link back before your teams use it.
outcome: Your plans, such as campaigns, create their Workfront projects from the agreed templates and stay linked to the work that tracks their progress.

steps: Agree with your Workfront administrator which custom forms, and which objects such as projects, need a Planning connection field.
Create the Planning connection custom fields and attach them to the agreed custom forms, then test them on a sample project.
Show your project teams where the connected records appear on a project, in a short session with a one-page guide.
deliverables: Planning connection fields on the agreed custom forms
Tested sample project
Walkthrough session and one-page guide
asks: Your Workfront administrator, to agree the custom forms and give us access
Project team members to join the walkthrough session
risk: Changes that surprise teams on live projects: we agree each form change with your administrator and test it on a sample project first.
outcome: Your project teams see the connected Workfront Planning records on their projects, from a field on the custom forms they already use.

steps: Agree the first event-triggered messages, such as cart, browse or welcome, and the scheduled sends, with the event, audience and profile attributes each one reads.
Set up each event-triggered message in Journey Optimizer to listen for its behavioral or system event and deliver a contextual message to the triggering profile.
Build the scheduled sends as campaigns on the agreed Real-Time CDP audiences, keeping sensitive attributes out unless you approve them.
Test entry, conditions and suppression for each message against an agreed set of test cases, including people who should not receive it, and record the results.
deliverables: Event-triggered messages for the agreed events
Scheduled sends on agreed Real-Time CDP audiences
Test cases and results for entry, conditions and suppression
asks: Your first messages, with the events, audiences and attributes each may use
Approved content for each message and the person who signs it off
risk: A message reaching the wrong people: we test entry, conditions and suppression with agreed test cases before any message reaches customers.
outcome: Your first event-triggered messages and scheduled sends run in Journey Optimizer on Real-Time CDP audiences and profile attributes, tested before they reach customers.

steps: Map each journey with your marketing team in a design sheet: its entry audience or event, branches, waits, conditions, exit criteria, and channel and content.
Build the journeys in Journey Optimizer, entering from the agreed Real-Time CDP audiences or events, with the waits, conditions and message actions from the design.
Set the exit criteria and the configured conditions that route each profile to the agreed channel and content.
Walk test cases through every branch, wait and exit before each journey goes live, and record the path each one took for your sign-off.
deliverables: Journey design sheets
Journeys built on Real-Time CDP audiences or events
Branch-by-branch test results
asks: A marketing lead who owns each journey and approves its design
Approved content for every message in each journey
risk: A profile stuck in a branch or sent too many messages: we test every path, wait and exit with test cases before each journey goes live.
outcome: Your branching, multi-touch journeys run in Journey Optimizer from Real-Time CDP audiences or events, routing each profile to the agreed channel and content.

steps: Build the offer catalog in Journey Optimizer Decisioning from an offer sheet agreed with your marketing team, naming the owner and intended audience of each offer.
Set the eligibility rules on Real-Time CDP audiences and attributes, keeping sensitive attributes out unless you approve them.
Configure the ranking strategies and placements, adding behavioral recommendation strategies where your catalog is large, so each profile gets the next-best offer or content.
Test the decisions with test cases for each audience, confirm that no profile receives an offer it is not eligible for, and review the rankings with your team.
deliverables: Offer catalog in Journey Optimizer Decisioning
Eligibility rules, ranking strategies and placements
Behavioral recommendation strategies, where the catalog is large
Decision test results
asks: Your offers and content, with an owner who approves each one
Your business rules for who may see each offer
Your rules on which attributes may be used to choose offers
risk: An offer shown to someone it was not meant for: we test eligibility rules with test cases for each audience before any placement goes live.
outcome: Your customers get the next-best offer or content from centralized decision logic in Journey Optimizer Decisioning, on the agreed placements across your channels.

steps: Agree the web and app surfaces to personalize, and what each one shows identified and anonymous visitors, in a personalization plan with your team.
Check that signed-in visits send a person-level identifier, such as a CRM ID or a hashed email, so Experience Platform stitches each visit into the profile.
Configure profile-based personalization for identified visitors on the agreed surfaces, delivering content, offers or promotions by real-time profile and segment membership.
Set up anonymous web personalization on captured behavioral signals and edge audiences, then test both paths with consent given and refused before launch.
deliverables: Personalization plan for the agreed surfaces
Profile-based personalization for identified visitors
Anonymous web personalization on edge audiences
Test results, with consent given and refused
asks: The web and app surfaces you want personalized, and who owns each
Approved content, offers and promotions for each audience
A developer who knows how your site and app send sign-in identifiers
risk: Personalization that ignores a visitor's consent choice: we test every surface with consent given and refused before it goes live.
outcome: Identified visitors see content, offers or promotions based on their real-time profile, and anonymous visitors see content based on their behavior on your site.

steps: Document with your data team the permitted collection and dataset route for the agreed concierge interaction data, without reusing the Brand Concierge-bundled datastream or dataset for other uses.
Test which clicks, form submissions, booked meetings and live chats arrive through that route, and record what each one carries.
Define the identity and XDM field mapping for each agreed signal, and record it in a mapping sheet your data team signs off.
Pilot the first agreed audience in Real-Time CDP from conversation signals and send it to the first agreed activation destination.
deliverables: Documented collection and dataset route
Inventory of the signals the route supplies
Identity and XDM field mapping
Pilot audience and activation destination
asks: A data team contact who owns your Experience Platform datasets and identities
Your privacy team's approval of each agreed use of conversation data
risk: Concierge data used beyond what is permitted: we document the route and each agreed use first, and your privacy team approves it before the pilot.
outcome: Agreed signals from your Brand Concierge conversations feed back into Real-Time CDP, with a first audience piloted for downstream personalization and activation.

steps: Agree with your marketing and privacy teams which Real-Time CDP profile attributes, behavioral signals and prior interactions the concierge may use, and which stay out.
Set up the agreed profile context for replies through the integration, keeping questions about a customer's own account on your secure channels.
Add test questions with ideal answers for known and anonymous visitors to the golden set, and score the replies against them with your reviewers.
Check that replies use only the agreed attributes and signals, and record the results for your sign-off before launch.
deliverables: Agreed list of attributes and signals the concierge may use
Golden-set test questions and scored replies
Sign-off record before launch
asks: Your privacy team's decision on which attributes and signals replies may use
Reviewers who score the test replies against the ideal answers
risk: A reply that reveals more about a customer than they expect: only agreed attributes are used, and the golden set must pass before launch.
outcome: Concierge replies draw on the Real-Time CDP context you approve, such as user attributes and prior interactions, tested against your golden set before launch.

steps: Agree with your marketing team the content engagement audiences to build, such as people who engaged with a given asset or experience attribute.
Build segments on Content Analytics asset and experience attributes in Workspace, and check their sizes with your team before publishing.
Publish the segments as audiences to Real-Time Customer Profile in Adobe Experience Platform, with clear names and descriptions.
Set up their activation in Real-Time CDP to the agreed destinations, under the data usage policies you enable, and confirm each audience arrives.
deliverables: Content engagement segments in Workspace
Audiences published to Real-Time Customer Profile
Activation set up in Real-Time CDP
asks: The content and creative themes your marketing team wants to target
The destinations where each audience should be activated
risk: Audiences too small or too broad to act on: we check each segment's size with your team in Workspace before publishing it.
outcome: People who engaged with chosen content and creative attributes become audiences you can activate in Real-Time CDP for targeting and personalization.

steps: Agree the sandbox, merge policy, connection and data views for audience analysis with your data team, and the audiences your analysts need.
Configure audience analysis on those choices, so audience membership from Profile datasets reaches your CJA connection as new dimensions.
Extend Adobe's Audience overview template with your KPIs, so your analysts compare audiences on the measures you already report.
Review the new audience dimensions with your analysts on an agreed set of audiences, and walk them through the extended template.
deliverables: Audience analysis configured for the agreed sandbox
Audience dimensions in the agreed data views
Audience overview template extended with your KPIs
Walkthrough for your analysts
asks: A data team contact who can agree the sandbox, merge policy and data views
Your KPIs and the audiences your analysts want to compare
risk: Analysts reading audiences from the wrong sandbox or merge policy: we agree each choice with your data team before we configure audience analysis.
outcome: Your analysts compare Real-Time CDP audiences in Customer Journey Analytics, with audience membership as dimensions and your own KPIs in the template.

steps: Review with your data team how each app identifies a person: the CJA person ID and stitching method, and the Real-Time CDP identity graph, in a side-by-side sheet.
Align the CJA person ID and stitching method with the Real-Time CDP identity graph, and record each choice and its reason.
Agree with your data team which datasets and retention windows each app uses, and compare audience counts for an agreed set of audiences.
Document the expected audience count differences and their causes in plain terms, and walk your stakeholders through them.
deliverables: Identity comparison sheet for both apps
Aligned CJA person ID and stitching method
Dataset and retention window agreement
Guide to expected audience count differences
asks: A data team contact who knows your identities and the datasets each app uses
The stakeholders who read audience counts, for a walkthrough
risk: Stakeholders losing trust when the two apps show different counts: we document the expected differences and their causes before anyone compares reports.
outcome: Your stakeholders know how Real-Time CDP and Customer Journey Analytics each define a person, and which audience count differences to expect and why.

steps: Agree up to five audiences with your marketing team, each defined by cross-channel journey behavior, with its intended use written down.
Define the audiences in CJA and check their sizes with your team before publishing.
Publish them to Adobe Experience Platform, so they arrive in Real-Time Customer Profile with clear names.
Set up their activation in Real-Time CDP with your team, to the agreed destinations, and confirm each audience arrives.
deliverables: Journey audiences defined in CJA
Audiences published to Adobe Experience Platform
Activation set up in Real-Time CDP
Audience definitions record
asks: The journeys and behaviors your marketing team wants to act on
The destinations where you want each audience activated
risk: Audiences defined on behavior too narrow to act on: we check each one's size with your team before it is published.
outcome: Audiences built on how people move across your channels in Customer Journey Analytics are activated through Real-Time CDP.

steps: Agree with your data and privacy teams the sandbox, marketing actions, consent rules and match keys, since the connection's settings apply to every audience sourced from it.
Create the Experience Platform data connection on the agreed sandbox, and set the marketing actions and consent rules.
Map identities and profile attributes to match keys with hashing, and schedule the refreshes.
Select the agreed audiences, then review each one in Real-Time CDP Collaboration after the first refresh and record the results for your sign-off.
deliverables: Experience Platform data connection
Match key and hashing map
Refresh schedule and selected audiences
Settings record with consent rules
asks: Your privacy team's approval of the marketing actions and consent rules
The audiences you want to make available to collaborators
A data team contact who knows your identities and profile attributes
risk: A wrong setting on the connection carries to every audience sourced from it: we agree each setting with your privacy team before selecting audiences.
outcome: Your chosen Real-Time CDP audiences are ready in Real-Time CDP Collaboration, matched on hashed keys under your consent rules and refreshed on schedule.

steps: Create the Experience Platform destination before any collaborator activates an audience, and agree the timing with your collaborators.
Map match keys to hashed identity namespaces, and set the linked keys and expiration agreed with your data team.
Apply data usage labels to the incoming audiences, so the data usage policies you enable apply when they are activated.
Check each shared audience in Audience Portal after the first activation, and record the results for your sign-off.
deliverables: Experience Platform destination for Real-Time CDP Collaboration
Match key, linked key and expiration settings
Data usage labels on shared audiences
Audience Portal check record
asks: A data team contact who can agree identity namespaces, linked keys and expiration
Your privacy team's choice of data usage labels
The planned activation dates from each collaborator
risk: A collaborator activating before the destination exists: we create it first and agree the activation timing with each collaborator.
outcome: Audiences your collaborators share arrive in Audience Portal on hashed identity namespaces, labeled for your data usage policies.

steps: Agree with your data team which conversion events count for campaign measurement, and the Experience Platform dataset that holds them.
Source the conversion event dataset from Experience Platform and map its identities to match keys.
Enrich the events with the agreed Real-Time Customer Profile attributes, and set the duplication key and conditions for attribution reports.
Reconcile the conversion events in Collaboration against your own records for an agreed period, and record the results for your sign-off.
deliverables: Conversion event dataset sourced to Collaboration
Identity to match key mapping
Duplication key and conditions for attribution reports
Reconciliation results
asks: Your definition of a conversion for each campaign you measure
A data team contact for the conversion dataset and its identities
risk: Conversions counted twice in attribution reports: we agree the duplication key and conditions with your team and reconcile counts before reports are shared.
outcome: Your conversion events feed the campaign measurement reports in Collaboration, matched on agreed keys and enriched with Real-Time Customer Profile attributes.

steps: Agree with your marketing and data teams the site events to collect and the identities they carry, recorded in an event map.
Map the site events to the XDM schema and datastream through the martech plugin, which loads Web SDK on your Edge Delivery pages.
Connect your consent platform, so Web SDK sends or discards data according to each visitor's consent, rather than a default of consent in.
Check on test visits that profiles build in Profile-enabled datasets under the agreed identities, viewing each customer profile in Adobe Experience Platform.
deliverables: Event map with identities
Site events mapped to the XDM schema and datastream
Consent platform connected to Web SDK
Test visit and profile check results
asks: Access to your Edge Delivery site's code and your consent platform
A data team contact who agrees the identities and the XDM schema
Your privacy team's sign-off on the events to collect
risk: Data collected without a visitor's consent: we connect your consent platform first and test visits with consent given and refused before launch.
outcome: Visits to your Edge Delivery pages build customer profiles in Experience Platform under the agreed identities, collected according to each visitor's consent.

steps: Agree with your marketing team the audiences editors will write for, and check that each one exists in your Real-Time CDP sandboxes.
Rename unclear audiences with your team's agreement, and check that the Audience list appears in Create for your editors.
Train your editors to choose an audience alongside a persona when they create content, with exercises on your own campaigns.
deliverables: Checked and clearly named audience list
Audience list available in Create
Editor training session and guide
asks: The audiences your marketing team wants editors to write for
Time from your editors for a training session
risk: Editors picking the wrong audience from unclear names: we agree clear names with your team before training and practice on your own campaigns.
outcome: Your editors choose Real-Time CDP audiences in GenStudio for Performance Marketing when they create content, so each piece is written for a customer segment.

steps: Read the touchpoint scores in Marketing Campaign Analytics with your marketing team to find the highest-value consumer segments, and agree which to target.
Rebuild each agreed segment as a base audience in Experience Platform on the default merge policy, and check its definition with your team.
Create lookalike audiences from the base audiences in Real-Time CDP, and review them with your team before activation.
Activate the lookalike audiences to the agreed destinations under the data usage policies you enable, and record each audience and its source segment.
deliverables: Shortlist of highest-value consumer segments
Base audiences in Experience Platform
Lookalike audiences, activated to agreed destinations
Record linking each lookalike to its segment
asks: A marketing lead who decides which segments to target
The destinations where the lookalike audiences should be activated
risk: A base audience that does not match its segment: we check each definition against the touchpoint scores with your team before creating lookalikes.
outcome: Lookalike audiences of your highest-value consumer segments are activated through Real-Time CDP, each traced back to the touchpoint scores behind it.

steps: List with your data team the conversion and event datasets already ingested for Real-Time CDP, such as CRM, commerce and web data, in a dataset inventory.
Check that identities are set up properly on each event dataset, and agree fixes with your data team where they are not.
Add the checked datasets as Marketing Campaign Analytics event inputs, and record each one's source and identities for your sign-off.
deliverables: Dataset inventory for campaign models
Identity check results for each event dataset
Event inputs set up in Marketing Campaign Analytics
asks: A data team contact who knows the datasets ingested for Real-Time CDP
Your list of the conversions that matter for campaign measurement
risk: Models built on event datasets with identity gaps: we check identities on each dataset and agree fixes before it becomes an input.
outcome: Marketing Campaign Analytics models run on the conversion and event data you already collect for Real-Time CDP, with identities checked on each dataset.

steps: Agree with your personalization team the audiences and profile attributes to share with Target for the first activities, keeping sensitive attributes out unless you approve them.
Configure the Adobe Target destination and its workspace in Real-Time CDP, using the datastream for your site.
Share the agreed audiences and profile attributes to the Adobe Target connection, and check that they appear in Target.
Walk your Target users through the shared audiences and attributes, ready for the first activities, such as A/B tests or Experience Targeting.
deliverables: Adobe Target destination and workspace configured
Agreed audiences and profile attributes shared to Target
Check record for the first activities
asks: Your personalization team's list of audiences and attributes for the first activities
A Target administrator who can name the workspace to use
risk: Sharing attributes that should stay private: we agree the attribute list with your team and share only those, checking each one in Target.
outcome: Your Real-Time CDP audiences and profile attributes are available in Target, ready for the first web and app personalization activities.

steps: Agree with your team the audiences that should qualify in real time, and the pages where same-page or next-page personalization applies.
Set up the datastream with the Target and Experience Platform services and edge segmentation, so the agreed audiences qualify in real time.
Run test visits to check that each agreed audience qualifies in real time and that its experience shows on the same page or the next.
Record the results and the datastream settings in a short runbook for your team.
deliverables: Datastream with Target, Experience Platform services and edge segmentation
Test visit results for each agreed audience
Datastream settings runbook
asks: The audiences and pages your team wants personalized in real time
Access to your datastream and to Target for the test visits
risk: An audience that qualifies too late for the visit it was meant for: we test each one with test visits before your team relies on it.
outcome: Visitors qualify for the agreed audiences in real time, so Target can personalize the page they are on or the next one they open.

steps: Agree the brands and onboarded domains to connect, and book time with the person on your side who has the right Google permissions.
Connect Search Console to each agreed brand's onboarded domain with a Google sign-in, and Google Analytics 4 where you do not have CJA, to fill the Business Impact tab.
Review the suggested queries with your team and pick the prompts to track by brand and market, since none are added automatically.
deliverables: Search Console connected for each agreed brand
Google Analytics 4 connected where you do not have CJA
Tracked prompt list by brand and market
asks: The person on your side with the right Google permissions for each domain
A marketing lead for each brand and market to help pick prompts
risk: Delays waiting for the right Google permissions: we agree who holds them for each domain first, and connect everything in one booked session.
outcome: Search Console is connected for each agreed brand, and Brand Visibility tracks prompts your team picked from real search queries, by brand and market.

steps: Activate Sites Optimizer on your production site, connect Google Search Console, and have your network team allow the IP addresses of Adobe's scanner in your CDN or firewall.
Set who can deploy fixes and who can prepare code patches, and name the developer who reviews, tests, merges and releases each patch.
Review the first SEO opportunities with your team, such as broken backlinks, metadata, structured data, sitemap issues and Core Web Vitals, and agree what to fix first.
Agree the route and owner for each kind of fix, deploy the first agreed content fixes into authoring or source documents, and prepare the code patches they need.
deliverables: Configured Sites Optimizer
Roles and approvals model
Route and owner for each kind of fix
Prioritized list of the first SEO fixes

A named developer who reviews, tests, merges and releases code patches
risk: Fixes published without review: content fixes go into authoring for your team to review and publish, and code patches go to your named developer.
outcome: Sites Optimizer runs on your production site, each kind of fix has a route and an owner, and the first agreed fixes are with your team.

steps: Add the event dataset and the Adobe Target Classification Events lookup dataset, which Adobe creates, to your CJA connection.
Add the activity and experience dimensions to the agreed data view, with the Experimentation context labels, and configure persistence for the Activity Name and Activity ID dimensions.
Build a first activity report in CJA with your team to check the dimensions, and record the setup in a short runbook.
Check each activity before launch: its type, and its reporting source set to CJA with the agreed data view, which cannot change once live.

Activity and experience dimensions with persistence and labels

risk: An activity launched with the wrong reporting source, which cannot change once live: we check every activity against a pre-launch checklist.
outcome: Your Target activities report in Customer Journey Analytics, with activity and experience dimensions ready for activity reports on the agreed data view.

steps: Agree the success metrics for Target activities with your optimization team, and how each one is defined in CJA.
Build Experimentation panel reports for your live Target activities, showing lift and confidence on the agreed success metrics.

Walk your optimization team through reading lift and confidence in the reports, using one of your own activities.

Reusable Workspace template
Agreed success metric definitions

steps: List your current Analytics for Target (A4T) activities by type with your optimization team, and agree which activity types move to CJA reporting.
Set the reporting source to CJA per activity or account wide, as agreed, and keep a record of which activities report where.
Give your Target users the Experience Platform role they need, and check that each one can open the new reports.
Show your team how activity reports in CJA compare with what they used in Adobe Analytics through A4T.
deliverables: Activity type transition plan
Reporting source set per activity or account wide
Experience Platform roles for Target users
Comparison walkthrough for your team

An administrator who can assign Experience Platform roles to your Target users
risk: Teams losing sight of results during the move: we agree which activity types move and when, and record where each activity reports.
outcome: The agreed Target activity types report in Customer Journey Analytics, your Target users have the access they need, and everyone knows where each activity reports.

steps: Agree with your personalization team the journey audiences to build in CJA and the personalization activities each one will serve.
Build the journey audiences in CJA, check their sizes with your team, and publish them to Experience Platform.
Share them with Target through the Adobe Target destination, in Real-Time CDP or Journey Optimizer, using a Target-enabled datastream.
Check that each audience appears in Target for the agreed personalization activities, and record each audience's definition and activities.

Audiences published to Experience Platform
Audiences shared through the Adobe Target destination

Access to your Target-enabled datastream and the Adobe Target destination
risk: Personalizing on audiences nobody can explain later: we record each audience's definition and the activities that use it, so your team can trace every experience.
outcome: Audiences built on journeys in Customer Journey Analytics reach Target for your agreed personalization activities, each one traced to its definition.

steps: Agree with your merchandising team the first tests on product, promotion or navigation content, each with a hypothesis and a success metric.
Map the agreed Commerce storefront events and attributes to supported Target parameters in your Target-enabled Web SDK implementation.
Build the first tests on the agreed store content, then check the mapping and the end-to-end behavior on your storefront before launch.

steps: Agree the route with your team: Web SDK, which Adobe recommends, or the martech plugin, which also needs Adobe Analytics and a Tags property.
Set up the datastream in Adobe Experience Platform that connects to Adobe Target, plus Adobe Analytics on the plugin route, and connect your consent platform.
Set up Target on the agreed Edge Delivery pages through the chosen route, and test each page with consent given and refused.
Check flicker and page speed on every agreed page before and after Target is added, and record the results for your sign-off.

steps: Agree with your marketing operations team which approved Workfront work should create content templates or fragments in Journey Optimizer, and what each one carries.
Set up the Journey Optimizer connection in Workfront Fusion with your Developer Console credentials, organization and sandbox, starting in a development sandbox for building and testing.
Build the scenario that creates the content templates or fragments when Workfront work is approved, using the Adobe Journey Optimizer modules.

Scenario that creates templates or fragments on approval

steps: Create the AI Reviewers in Workfront setup and set them to use Adobe Brand Intelligence, with names your reviewers will recognize.
Choose a sample of real assets with your brand team, including some known to break your brand rules.

outcome: AI Reviewers in Workfront review assets with Adobe Brand Intelligence, and your brand team has checked their comments against what Validate reports.

steps: Add the AI Reviewer to your approval templates, so the brand check runs on every request that uses them.
Agree with your brand and project leads what happens when an asset fails the check, and write it into a one-page process.
Train your project coordinators and approvers to read the AI Reviewer's comments before their own review, using assets from your own requests.

Agreed process for assets that fail
Training for coordinators and approvers
asks: Your list of approval templates the brand check should run on
Brand and project leads to agree what happens when an asset fails
Time from your coordinators and approvers for a training session

steps: Review your Workfront access levels and sharing with your Workfront system administrator, since CX Enterprise Coworker Chat works within each user's permissions.
Decide with your governance board when to turn on write access, and have your administrator enable the Write MCP tools option in System Preferences at that point.
Write a starter prompt library for your own processes with the teams who run them, giving the expected result for each prompt.
Pilot the library with one team for an agreed period, collect their feedback, and revise the prompts before a wider rollout.

Record of the write access decision
Starter prompt library for your processes
Pilot feedback and revised prompts

Time with your governance board to decide on write access
One team willing to pilot the prompt library

steps: Agree the first scenarios with your creative operations team: which Workfront requests start them, the prompt or source image each takes, and who reviews the results.
Create the Adobe Firefly connection in Workfront Fusion with your Developer Console credentials.
Build the scenarios that take the prompt or source image from each request, generate, expand or fill images, and attach the results to the same work for review.
Test each scenario on sample requests, check the results with your reviewers, and hand over a runbook for errors and changes.

First image generation scenarios
Sample request test results
Runbook for errors and changes

The Workfront request types and reviewers for the first scenarios

outcome: Workfront requests with a prompt or source image get generated, expanded or filled images back on the same work, ready for your reviewers.

steps: List the repeat edits your creative team makes on files tied to Workfront tasks, such as composites, Photoshop actions and renditions, and agree which to automate first.
Add the current Adobe Photoshop modules to your Workfront Fusion scenarios for the agreed edits, with the settings taken from each request.
Move any older scenarios onto the current modules, and test each one against its previous output on the same files.
Check the edited files returned to each task with your creative team, and record the scenarios in a runbook.

Older scenarios moved onto current modules
Before and after test results
Scenario runbook

steps: Check with your administrators that Workfront and GenStudio sit in the same organization and that every reviewer is a user of both.

Have each reviewer install the Workfront web viewer extension, then run a test review from request to decision and check the decision shows in GenStudio.

Role map from GenStudio roles to Workfront license types
Test review record, from request to decision

Your reviewers' time to install the web viewer extension and join a test

outcome: Content created in GenStudio is reviewed and approved in Workfront Proof, and the decision shows in GenStudio before anything is published.

steps: Agree with your content leads, in an approval matrix, who reviews and approves each kind of content and by when.

Attach the templates to the Workfront projects your editors choose from in GenStudio, and test one review for each kind of content.
Train your editors and approvers on the proofing viewer, with a short guide to commenting and deciding.
